claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, which the cloud provider enforces independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (Pulumi property) that provides deletion protection enforced by the cloud provider.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (Pulumi property) that provides deletion protection enforced by the cloud provider.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` not set) and still refuse to delete because of provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while not having provider-side deletion protection.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section titled 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider-side deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, which the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi (i.e., Pulumi itself refuses to delete the protected resource), independent of any cloud-side deletion protection.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute (a deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect`).
An AWS RDS instance resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute (a deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect`).
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attribute (such as `deletionProtection`) are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The destroy-failures troubleshooting page (/docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/) has a section titled 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself).

The 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' section of the destroy-failures troubleshooting page explains how to tell Pulumi `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.

A `pulumi destroy` failure is often caused by the resource itself being guarded against deletion rather than by an engine problem, and something has to remove that guard before Pulumi can delete the resource.

Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection for a resource (Pulumi's `protect` option, a provider-enforced flag, and a cloud-API-enforced protection), and the error message usually indicates which layer was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When a `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error message names a URN and mentions `protect`.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` is a provider-enforced flag that makes the Pulumi provider refuse to issue the delete call.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi, for example AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, or an Azure Resource Manager management lock.

When a cloud API enforces deletion protection, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (as for an Azure Resource Manager management lock).
The remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection is the same.
`pulumi destroy` deletes the resources recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently says.
Setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program is not enough on its own for `pulumi destroy` to succeed; the program change must first be applied with `pulumi up`.
Running `pulumi up` after setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` propagates the change to both the live resource and Pulumi's state.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (for example directly in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality, and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`.
A non-empty `aws.s3.BucketV2` fails to delete unless `forceDestroy` is set to `true`.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute (EC2 termination protection) that is enforced by the AWS API.
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `aws.dynamodb.Table` defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and its scope-specific variants (for example `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`) are the Pulumi Azure Native resources for management locks.
Azure Resource Manager enforces management locks independent of anything in the Pulumi program; a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the locked resource can be deleted.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name as a soft-deleted vault fails with the error `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
